name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth (Sigismund III)

areaKm2.note: world_1600 Poland-Lithuania polygon = 889,709 km2 on the sphere. Commonly quoted ~990,000 km2 after Deulino (1619) incl. Smolensk; ~815,000 km2 c. 1582.

population.note: Military Revolution article gives 11M for the Commonwealth c. 1650 (tacitus.nu). HYDE modern-border values for 1600 (OWID): Poland 5.0M, Belarus 0.72M, Lithuania 0.11M (too low), Ukraine 3.4M (only partly inside); Frost (Northern Wars, isbn:0-582-06429-5) ~8-10M c. 1600 in ~815,000-990,000 km2. Mid 9.5M.

urbanization.note: OWID urban share: Poland 7.6% (1600), falling to 4.3% (1700). Lithuania and Ruthenia much less urban. Mid 6%.

activePersonnel.note: Under arms in 1610: the royal army besieging Smolensk (~12,000 under Sigismund and Zolkiewski in 1609, Polish-Russian War article), Zolkiewski's field force at Klushino 6,500-6,800 (Battle of Klushino article), the Lithuanian army in Livonia (~5,000-8,000), the quarter army on the southern frontier (~2,500 cavalry in peacetime, Wojsko kwarciane article), plus Zaporozhian Cossacks and Lisowczycy mercenaries serving for pay (~10,000-15,000).

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: the pospolite ruszenie (noble levy, theoretically 50,000-100,000 horse, rarely called and slow) and magnate private troops; registered Cossacks beyond those serving.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess: artillery and siege train at Smolensk, train and administration; no navy.

mobilizationRatio.note: Military Revolution article (Parker/Nolan): 17,000-53,000 under arms c. 1630-1650 for 11M people (0.2-0.5%); with the noble levy and Cossacks the wartime ceiling was ~1.5-2.5%.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Winged hussars: most of Zolkiewski's 6,500-6,800 at Klushino were hussars (Battle of Klushino article); more with the royal army and the Lithuanian forces (Kircholm 1605).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75-1.0. Evidence: long kopia lance, half-armour, fine horses: the best shock cavalry of the era (Kircholm 1605, Klushino 1610)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: nobles trained from youth in companies with retainers (pocztowi)

count.note: Pancerni/cossack-style companies, Tatar companies and the Lisowczycy light horse (Polish-Russian War article).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: mail, bow, sabre, firearms

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: experienced frontier companies; Lisowczycy undisciplined

count.note: Educated guess: Hungarian-style hajduk infantry and German-style foreign infantry (piechota niemiecka) and wybraniecka infantry with the royal army.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical) to 0.75 (among the era best). Evidence: hajduk arquebusiers, few pikes

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: mercenary and hired companies

count.note: Educated guess: Zaporozhian Cossack infantry serving at Smolensk (estimates range ~10,000-30,000 with large uncertainty).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: samopal guns, tabor tactics

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: irregulars, good in sieges and wagon forts

count.note: Educated guess: a weak siege train at Smolensk (the siege lasted 20 months); Zolkiewski had 2 guns at Klushino (Battle of Klushino article).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: few heavy guns, Crown arsenal small

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: hired gunners

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75. Evidence: Zolkiewski (Klushino) and Chodkiewicz (Kircholm) were among the best commanders of the era; hetman system independent of the king, poor coordination of the siege of Smolensk

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: hussar companies strong, but pay arrears caused confederations (mutinies) such as 1612-13

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75. Evidence: Kircholm (1605) and Klushino (1610); Polish garrison in the Kremlin from Sept 1610

weapons.note: Anchor: 5 (1600). Evidence: firearms mixed with lance and bow; strong cavalry, weak infantry firepower

armor.note: Anchor: 5 (half-armor). Evidence: hussar half-armour and mail

ships.note: Anchor: 4 (cogs, galleys). Evidence: no royal fleet beyond privateers (a small fleet was only built 1620s)

fortification.note: Anchor: 4.7. Evidence: Kamianets and a few bastioned works; most towns medieval-walled

logistics.note: Anchor: 4.6. Evidence: tabor wagon trains, river transport on the Vistula and Dnieper

communications.note: Anchor: 4.6. Evidence: courier posts; royal post Krakow-Venice

isr.note: Anchor: ISR uses the same years as the anchor table (1600 -> 5, 1805 -> 6). Evidence: cavalry screens, spies and merchant reports only; no aerial or signal intelligence

air.note: No aircraft or military balloons before 1783/1794.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (2011 int$): Poland 1600 = 1,038, 1610 = 995, 1620 = 872. Lithuania and Ruthenia poorer; mid = Poland 1610 value.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: the kwarta (a quarter of crown-land income) and taxes voted by the Sejm; the state was fiscally weak, armies went unpaid.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: grain-export economy; crafts in Gdansk and Krakow, salt mines (Wieliczka).

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: the granary of Europe; Gdansk exported ~100,000+ tons of rye a year c. 1600-20.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.009-0.011 (mid 0.0095): in a pre-transition age structure (Wrigley and Schofield type, life expectancy ~30-35) males reaching 18 each year are about 0.9-1.1% of total population. Males only.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: unpaved tracks; Vistula, Neman and Dnieper the main arteries.

majorPorts.note: Gdansk (semi-autonomous), Riga (until 1621), Elblag, Konigsberg (ducal Prussia, a fief).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: Gdansk shipping; most grain left on Dutch hulls.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: cavalry armies with wagon trains and requisition could raid deep (Klushino, Moscow 1610) but sieges starved for funds.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horse-rich szlachta estates, oxen for the grain trade; Ukrainian steppe horse herds.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain and cavalry mobility, but few fortresses and open plains; 1.3 only in the forest-marsh east and in winter.

notes: Snapshot = 1610, the year of Klushino (4 July) and the Polish occupation of Moscow, siege of Smolensk under way. Population: Crown of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania incl. Ruthenian Ukraine; ducal Prussia and Livonian vassals excluded. Personnel convention: the quarter army, wartime paid companies, Lisowczycy and paid Cossacks are active; the pospolite ruszenie (noble levy) and magnate private armies are trainedReserves. Infantry and Cossack counts are weak (grade D). No navy.
